headline: Check Point gateways, an N-central zero-day and a PostgreSQL RCE dominate patch urgency
standfirst: Actively exploited flaws in Check Point gateways and N-able N-central lead the day, while PostgreSQL’s latest update fixes an authenticated code-execution bug. Police disruption, GitHub account abuse, DPRK crypto theft and telecom interception round out the picture.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

Check Point gateways are the lead story: PHP2Shell was used for initial compromise, while CVE-2026-123039 let attackers elevate to root in destructive attacks [[s32]]. The flaw is a High-severity 7.8 permission-assignment issue in which the Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon listens on a world-writable local socket without authenticating connecting processes; an authenticated local user can have commands executed as root. CISA lists it in KEV and sets a federal remediation deadline, which raises urgency but does not create a universal one. The local, authenticated precondition matters: this is not a remote unauthenticated path.

N-able’s N-central zero-day, dubbed 4EverAble2Shell, was exploited within hours of a PoC release to compromise servers and deploy cryptocurrency miners, with researchers reporting at least 21 affected systems, including 19 running the latest security update [[s41]]. No CVE was supplied. Analysis: that concentration on current builds makes patch-bypass risk the immediate question for MSPs, though the excerpt does not explain the mechanism.

## Vulnerabilities

PostgreSQL’s latest release fixes 52 flaws, including CVE-2026-6460, a 22-year-old type-confusion bug that lets a database user who can create objects execute code as the OS user running the database [[s4]]. It is High severity at 8.8 with a network vector but low privileges required, and NVD lists versions before 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25 as affected. Full protection also requires rebuilding C-language extensions. No KEV entry was supplied. Separately, Nightmare Eclipse released a Windows zero-day exploit called SignDrop that abuses CLFS and Windows Defender to trigger arbitrary file creation in the context of the antimalware process [[s28]]. No CVE, affected versions or patch status were supplied. The significance is the attack path itself: a Defender-context file write is a primitive defenders should track, but the excerpt does not establish in-the-wild exploitation.

## Industry

Operation Endgame took down servers behind Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC, and police seized about 6.4 million stolen logins belonging to more than 40,000 victims, according to Germany’s BKA [[s21]]. The tools were used for access, password theft and ransomware, so the disruption targets infrastructure that feeds criminal access and extortion.

## Breaches

The wfx-loot campaign used 4,837 compromised GitHub accounts to probe 61,764 repositories, open pull requests and push secrets-stealing malware [[s37]]. The scale is the story: cloud credentials are the prize, and repository write access is the delivery mechanism. Analysis: that combination is a supply-chain risk for organizations whose code depends on GitHub, though the excerpt does not name victims or estimate credential loss. The FBI attributes more than $400 million in cryptocurrency theft to DPRK-tied actors running a social-engineering scheme codenamed FaceStealer, using deepfake video calls [[s12]]. The alleged campaign ran over an 18-month span and is part of a coordinated set of U.S. government actions. The attribution is the FBI’s, not an independent assessment in the excerpt. Analysis: the case reinforces that deepfake-assisted social engineering can convert trust into direct financial loss, but no technical indicators were supplied.

## Research

Enea named SilentAir, a spying group it assesses with high confidence to be state-level, after finding attack sources inside mobile operators in at least six Asian countries [[s20]]. The group used hacked equipment to intercept calls and texts, including SMS 2FA codes, for selected people, mostly in Taiwan. Analysis: operator-level interception is a direct challenge to SMS-based second factors for targeted users, though the excerpt does not detail how targets were selected.

kev.vulnerabilityName: Check Point Multiple Products Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: Check Point Firewall, Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Scalable Platforms, Security Gateway, and Security Management Server contain an incorrect permissions assignment for critical resources vulnerability when the Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon runs as root and listens on a world-writable local socket without authenticating connecting processes. An authenticated local user can send a command to the socket and have it executed as root.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description: The Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon runs as root and listens on a world-writable local socket (/tmp/dynamic_socket) without authenticating connecting processes. An authenticated local user can send a command to the socket and have it executed as root.

selected.angle: Check Point gateways are being exploited in the wild to gain root and wipe ESXi hosts, and CISA's KEV deadline of Nov. 16 makes patching urgent.

Any code run this way has the rights of the operating

nvd.description: Type confusion in PostgreSQL allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via ALTER ... SET DATA TYPE primarily.  Other DDL attack routes exist, such as "ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN; ROLLBACK; ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN".  The system had inadequate tracking of typed values, and values were not self-identifying.  Stale values could appear in data dictionary entries, PL/pgSQL variables, and many other parts of the system.  PostgreSQL Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

selected.angle: PostgreSQL's 52 fixes include an authenticated RCE in versions before 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25, so admins must patch and rebuild C extensions.
